open-question.question: What is the file name of the new task-list tool under core/tools/, the name every runtime command, CLAUDE.md invariant, doc entry, and test fixture will carry (define_milestone.py and open_questions.py are the two existing precedents)?
open-question.alternative: Name the tool core/tools/task_list.py: a document-named noun in the open_questions.py style, singular, taken from the "task list" / "task-list tool" wording the milestone goal, the skill descriptions, and docs already use for TASKS_TODO.md and TASKS_DONE.md together. Every runtime command reads python3 {{PLUGIN_ROOT}}/tools/task_list.py <subcommand> <MILESTONE_DIR> …, and tests and the conftest runner take the matching task_list prefix. It matches the vocabulary already in place: "task list" and "task-list" are the most frequent terms in core/ and docs/ for these files, and the milestone itself calls the thing the task-list tool, so the name needs no explanation in CLAUDE.md, the docs, or a skill step, and subcommands like move, insert, and append read naturally after a noun, as they do after open_questions.py. The singular names one list while the tool writes two files, and "task list" in prose often means TASKS_TODO.md alone (complete-all-tasks works "the task list"), so the name slightly understates that the move spans both files.

Name the tool core/tools/task_lists.py: a document-named noun in the open_questions.py style, plural like open_questions.py, naming both task files the tool writes as the two task lists. Commands read python3 {{PLUGIN_ROOT}}/tools/task_lists.py <subcommand> <MILESTONE_DIR> …, with tests and the conftest runner under the task_lists prefix. It mirrors the closest precedent exactly (a plural noun naming the documents the tool is the sole writer of, the subcommands carrying the verbs) and states in the name that one tool owns both TASKS_TODO.md and TASKS_DONE.md, which is what the sole-writer invariant in CLAUDE.md will say. "Task lists" is a rarer form in the existing prose than "task list", and task_list.py versus task_lists.py is an easy one-letter slip in the many fixed commands written into runtime prose, where a typo fails at run time rather than in the build.

Name the tool core/tools/tasks.py: a document-named noun taken from the TASKS_ prefix the two files share, the shortest form. Commands read python3 {{PLUGIN_ROOT}}/tools/tasks.py <subcommand> <MILESTONE_DIR> …, with tests and the conftest runner under the tasks prefix. It ties the name directly to the file names it writes (TASKS_TODO.md, TASKS_DONE.md) and keeps every fixed command, including the long chained completion call shown in full in runtime prose, as short as possible. The word "tasks" is everywhere in the runtime prose, docs, and test names, so searching for the tool's call sites or test files by its name is noisy, and a bare tasks.py on the pytest pythonpath is a generic module name that says less about what the file is than either existing tool's name does.

Name the tool core/tools/write_tasks.py: an act-named verb_noun in the define_milestone.py style, the verb naming the tool's role as the only writer of the task files (reads stay prose, per the goal). Commands read python3 {{PLUGIN_ROOT}}/tools/write_tasks.py <subcommand> <MILESTONE_DIR> …, with tests and the conftest runner under the write_tasks prefix. The name itself carries the milestone's central claim, that this tool writes and nothing else does, and signals at every call site that reads of TASKS_TODO.md and TASKS_DONE.md do not go through it. define_milestone.py is a single-act tool with no subcommands, so this follows its form but not its shape: a verb name over verb subcommands reads doubled (write_tasks.py move, write_tasks.py insert), and a read subcommand added later, such as a heading listing, would contradict the name.

open-question.question: When the task-list tool is given a task title (the section to move, or a before/after anchor), does it match it exactly after whitespace- and case-folding, refusing anything else so a partial task name is resolved by the runner's own read of TASKS_TODO.md before the call, or does it carry the completion procedure's case-insensitive partial match itself, which then needs a rule for two sections matching and a way to tell the runner which heading it took?

In what form does the move subcommand read the derived acceptance bar on standard input: one criterion per non-empty line, criteria separated by blank lines so a criterion wrapped over several lines folds to one bullet, or already-rendered "- " bullets the tool checks and copies under the **Verified:** label?

Does the task-list tool parse a whole task file and re-render it in one canonical layout on every write, normalizing the blank-line convention of every section it did not touch, or does it splice only the bytes of the section it adds or removes and leave every other byte of the file as it stands?

When a task file holds a ## section with no trailing --- separator before the next ## heading or the end of the file, does the tool refuse the call with an Error: line and the files unchanged, or treat the next heading or the end of file as that section's end?

Does the task-list tool refuse a write that would leave two sections with the same folded title in one task file (an insert or append of a title TASKS_TODO.md already holds, or a move into a TASKS_DONE.md already holding an entry of that title), or does it write what it is given and leave title uniqueness to the authoring prose as today?
open-question.alternative: The tool enforces no title uniqueness on any write: insert, append, and move write the section they are given whatever titles the target file already holds, and uniqueness stays an authoring duty of the prose alone (task-format.md's "unique within the file" guideline, submit-task's duplicate triage, derive-tasks' skip of work already in TASKS_DONE.md), with no check added now or planned for later. Smallest tool with no new refusal path or test surface, and it guards against a failure that has not occurred: a scan of all 46 milestone directories finds no folded title repeated within any TASKS_TODO.md or TASKS_DONE.md and none present in both files of one milestone, so the prose has held so far. A duplicate the prose misses is written silently and only surfaces later, at completion, where two sections answer the same title and the move takes whichever the matching rule resolves (or refuses then, after the task's work is already done); the goal makes the tool the sole writer, yet the one structural property the move depends on stays unchecked by it. How harmful this is depends on the sibling question on the title matching rule.

The tool refuses, with one Error: line and both files unchanged, any insert or append (initialize-then-append in derive-tasks included) whose folded title equals a section TASKS_TODO.md already holds; a move into TASKS_DONE.md is never checked against existing done entries, and no cross-file check is made at authoring time. Guards exactly the file where uniqueness is load-bearing — the completion procedure locates a pending task by its heading in TASKS_TODO.md — and refuses at authoring time, before any work has been done on the task, while the move, the step that runs after a task's work is finished, gains no failure mode of its own. TASKS_DONE.md can end up holding two entries of one title (a task re-submitted after its first copy completed), so the done log stops being keyed by title for any reader that looks an entry up by heading, such as capture or ask-in-milestone-context; a refused append also has to be handled inside derive-tasks' write call, whose shape the sibling question on derive append granularity owns.

The tool refuses, with one Error: line and both files unchanged, any write that would leave two sections of the same folded title in one task file: an insert or append of a title TASKS_TODO.md already holds, and a move into a TASKS_DONE.md already holding an entry of that title; a new TODO title that only matches a done entry is not checked at authoring time. Makes "unique within the file" a property both task files hold by construction, one symmetric rule stated once in the tool and pinned by tests, so every reader of either file can key a section by its title without trusting the authoring prose. A title already present in TASKS_DONE.md passes the authoring check and is then refused at the move, after the completer has done the work and derived the bar, leaving a finished task stuck in TASKS_TODO.md with no tool path to rename it; the runner's recovery from that refusal (and whether the agent may retitle the section) has to be written into the completion prose.

The tool refuses, with one Error: line and both files unchanged, an insert or append whose folded title equals a section in either TASKS_TODO.md or TASKS_DONE.md, and also refuses a move into a TASKS_DONE.md already holding an entry of that title, so one title names at most one section across the milestone's two task files. Catches every collision at authoring time, before any work is spent, including a re-submission of an already completed task's title, so the move-time refusal can only fire on files a writer outside the tool has disturbed and both files stay keyed by title. Widest check: insert and append must read and parse TASKS_DONE.md too, so a malformed done file (an unterminated section, whose handling the sibling question on unterminated sections owns) can now block authoring a new task, and it refuses a deliberate re-run of a completed task under its old title, forcing the author to invent a distinguishing title for legitimate follow-up work.

open-question.question: Beyond refusing an empty title or body, does the task-list tool validate an authored section against task-format.md (title of 4 to 8 title-cased words, a 1 to 3 sentence body, no sub-heading or labeled section inside the body), or does it accept any body text as the section's prose and leave the format to the authoring skills?

When derive-tasks initializes TASKS_TODO.md through the tool and the file already holds ## sections, does the tool refuse unless an explicit flag confirms the replacement, or replace the contents silently as the skill does today?

Inside its one shell call, does derive-tasks write its ordered briefs as one tool process per brief (each brief its own quoted heredoc, refused alone while the rest land), or as one tool process that takes the whole ordered list on standard input and writes it or refuses it as a whole?

Which file shows the completion tail's one fixed shell call in full (the move subcommand chained with the runner's own git step), given that the shared completion procedure stays commit-free and the git step differs between the complete-task agent (its path-scoped git add) and the inline skill (the commit procedure's three steps): the procedure's step 5 with the git step as a per-runner placeholder, or each wrapper with the procedure reduced to the tool command alone?

When a before or after anchor title names no section in TASKS_TODO.md, does the tool refuse the call with an Error: line so submit-task re-calls with append and prints its one-line advisory itself, or does the tool append the section in that call and print the fallback advisory in the runner's place, breaking the rule that a mutator prints nothing on success?

When the move has replaced one of the two task files and the replacement of the other then fails, which state does the tool leave: both files unchanged, by rendering both before replacing either and restoring the first on a failed second replace, or the harmless superset with the entry appended to TASKS_DONE.md and the section still standing in TASKS_TODO.md, in the order the answer core's fold-before-remove uses?
open-question.alternative: The move renders both new file contents in memory before touching either, replaces TASKS_DONE.md first and TASKS_TODO.md second through the existing same-directory temporary-file writer, and if the second replace fails it writes TASKS_DONE.md's original bytes back through the same writer, so the call ends with one Error: line, exit 1, and both files byte-for-byte as they were. Only if that restore also fails does the superset (entry in TASKS_DONE.md, section still in TASKS_TODO.md) remain, and the Error: line then says so. A re-run after a clean failure is an ordinary move. Keeps the tools' shared contract intact without an exception: every failure leaves the files unchanged, exactly as open_questions.py and define_milestone.py promise and test_contract.py pins, so a retry of the chained call needs no repair step and the runner's git step, chained behind the tool, never sees a half-moved pair. Adds a rollback path the other tools never needed (each writes one file), which is hard to exercise in tests without injecting a failure between the two replaces, and its guarantee still degrades to the superset on a double failure, so the contract has to name that edge anyway.

The move renders both new contents first, then replaces TASKS_DONE.md (entry with its Verified bar appended) before TASKS_TODO.md (section removed), mirroring the answer core's fold-before-remove; if the second replace fails it leaves the superset in place with no rollback and prints one Error: line naming that TASKS_DONE.md was written and TASKS_TODO.md was not, exit 1. The tool's every-failure-leaves-files-unchanged contract gains this one stated exception; recovery is left to the runner or the user (removing the duplicate by hand or restoring TASKS_DONE.md from git), and a retried move gets no special handling. The simplest code with a failure state that never loses work: the section and the derived bar both survive on disk, the order matches the fold-before-remove precedent the project already reasons with, and the chained git step does not run, so nothing half-moved is staged or committed. Breaks the uniform unchanged-on-failure contract with a per-subcommand exception, and a straightforward retry would append a second entry of the same title to TASKS_DONE.md or be refused, depending on how the task-title-uniqueness sibling settles, so the interrupted state needs a manual repair before the task can be recorded again.

The same DONE-first, TODO-second order with no rollback and the same Error: line on a failed second replace, plus a resume rule: when a move is called for a title whose section still stands in TASKS_TODO.md and whose entry already stands in TASKS_DONE.md, the tool treats the earlier move as interrupted and completes it by removing the section from TASKS_TODO.md only, keeping the existing DONE entry and its bar rather than writing the newly piped one. The interrupted state heals by simply re-running the same chained call, so neither the runner nor the user ever hand-edits a task file, and no work is lost at any point. Adds a second code path and a detection rule that can misfire when a TASKS_DONE.md entry of the same folded title is not actually this task's interrupted move, and silently drops the re-run's freshly piped bar; its safety depends on how the task-title-uniqueness and task-title-matching siblings settle, since both govern what counts as the same title.

open-question.question: Does the new tool repeat the stdin reader, ToolError, the one-Error-line main, and the atomic same-directory writer as its own standalone single file, as define_milestone.py does with a parity test that it imports neither sibling, or do the three tools now share one helper module under core/tools/ that the build copies beside them?
